timeline.description: Computational workflow: (1) Geometry optimizations with wB97XD/6-31G(d); (2) Frequency calculations for thermal corrections at 298 K; (3) Single-point energies at wB97XD/6-311G(d,p); (4) Solvation free energy with SMD in butyl ethanoate; (5) Calculation of Gibbs free energies and redox potentials via Nernst equation.

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper explicitly describes this computational workflow in the Methodology section (page 3). It states: geometries optimized at wB97XD/6-31G(d); vibrational frequency calculations at the same level to obtain thermal corrections for Gibbs free energy at 298 K; single-point electronic energies at wB97XD/6-311G(d,p); solvation free energies computed using SMD continuum solvation; solvent chosen as butyl ethanoate; and redox potentials computed from Gibbs free energies using the Nernst equation (eq 1). These steps match the extracted timeline.

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper does not describe oxidation/reduction potentials for the polymers only “qualitatively without explicit numeric values.” In fact, it explicitly provides numeric values (or explicit numeric ESW/oxidation/reduction potentials) for the pristine polymers and discusses them in text.
